Priya K: Acme POC returns 403 only when requests route through their corporate proxy. Direct calls to api.redwood.dev work. Anyone seen proxies strip X-Redwood- headers?
Alex S: Paste failing curl (redact key) + x-request-id.
Priya K: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate"
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"invalid_org_claim","message":"org claim missing or mismatched"}
x-request-id: rq_demo_77

Alex S: That error means our auth didn't see the org claim. Can you get the upstream proxy logs for rq_demo_77?
Jin L: Many enterprise proxies (Zscaler, Blue Coat) drop or normalize non-standard headers. Also watch underscores vs hyphens.
Priya K: they run Zscaler + an internal nginx forward proxy. Their nginx upstream request doesn't include X-Redwood-Org.
Alex S: Options: 1) have them allowlist our header (best), 2) switch to hyphenated header name, 3) short-lived scoped API key bound to acme-corp so header not required.
Priya K: they can't change proxy rules today. Can we issue a scoped demo key for the POC?
Alex S: Yes. I'll create a 24h demo-scoped key and DM it. Log it as a temporary workaround.
deploy-bot: created demo_key_acme_24h (expires in 24h)
Sam R: OK for demo with expiry; ensure trial limits and note in deal tracker.
Jin L: I'll draft a KB with nginx and Envoy examples (proxy_set_header, header whitelist notes) and a tcpdump grep to show missing X-Redwood-Org. Add fallback patterns (scoped key, org-in-jwt, subdomain).
Priya K: Customer validated the demo flow with the temp key. They'll schedule a network window next week for allowlist. Closing for now; will reopen if we see more 403s. Thanks :thumbsup:
